Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 16)
Topic: Welcome to Ashaeiynn — The Four Rules for Every Member , and the Monthly AuraChecking Pr ocess

Sour ce: A live welcoming addr ess deliver ed during an ongoing hawan (fir e ritual) session at Ashaeiynn (video transcript, ~46 min) — addr essed to brand-new members and existing sangat together . Explains why members wer e br ought her e, lays out four essential rules every practitioner must follow , and covers practical announcements about the monthly aura-checking ("ora checking") pr ocess, followed by extensive live sangat Q&A on both spiritual and practical topics. Purpose: Chatbot knowledge — English version.
1. WHY YOU'RE HERE — YOUR OWN PRAYERS BROUGHT YOU

No one arrives at Ashaeiynn pur ely by their own choice. Every person here has, at some point, prayed to their Gurudev , their devta, or the Parmeshwar — and the very proof of that prayer is that you are at Ashaeiynn today . You wer e sent here on your own devta's orders , ultimately as a result of your own past prayers, your own tattva, and your own past karmas — meaning you already have a deep, pre-existing relationship with this place. The task now is simply to recognize that relationship.
2. YOUR FIRST TASK — LEARN TO UNDERSTAND THE SUKSHMA JAGA T (SUBTLE WORLD)

The first job for anyone arriving at Ashaeiynn is learning HOW to understand the sukshma jagat. Every activity happening in the subtle world will be taught here — whatever is necessary for opening drishti (spiritual sight), and whatever facts about the subtle world a practitioner needs, will all be covered at Ashaeiynn.
3. ASHAEIYNN WORKS CONTINUOUSLY — MENTORS AND SHAKTIS AVAILABLE 24/7

Ashaeiynn functions all seven days, 24 hours a day — whether in the physical (sthool) world or the subtle (sukshma) world, it remains continuously active in service of the Guru. Ashaeiynn's shaktis and mentors ar e ready ar ound the clock to help members — new arrivals are asked to stay in contact with their assigned mentor .
4. RULE ONE — ACCEPT HANUMAN JI MAHARAJ AS GURU

Members were sent here specifically to Gurudev Shri Hanuman Ji Maharaj, who will guide them until their primary connection ("prime milan") with their own devta is established. Hanuman Ji Maharaj functions here in the role of Guru, and always retains that "guru tattva." First rule: accept Hanuman Ji Maharaj as Guru. Whether or not a person consciously accepts this doesn't change the underlying mechanism — since a person arrives at Ashaeiynn precisely because of their own devta, their own tattva, and their own past karmas, that deep connection to this place already exists regardless of belief.
5. WHY LEARN FROM THE GURU — REAWAKENING PAST-LIFE VIDYAS, NOT NEW DEVOTION

Members ar e not being taught devotion to God — they ar e alr eady devotees of God. If someone were not already a devotee, they would not be here at all. What IS being taught: the sukshma jagat vidyas a person alr eady learned in a P AST life. Everyone present learned confidential (gopniya) subtle-world vidyas in previous births; the purpose of being called here now is specifically to reawaken that dormant knowledge. Ashaeiynn simply consolidates and delivers those same vidyas, under Gurudev Shri Hanuman Ji Maharaj's own direction.
6. SHAKTI KA SIDDHANT — THE JAI SIY A RAM MANTRA AS FOUNDATION

The entire principle of shakti (power) at Ashaeiynn runs thr ough the Jai Siya Ram mantra. This shakti is fully awakened, and remains bound and connected, through this mantra together with the vows/prayers taught in the app or by mentors — the same vows and prayers that bind and awaken the sants, mahatmas, and shaktis associated with this place.
7. THE PROGRAMMER ANALOGY — LEARN BASIC TOOLS BEFORE INNOVATING

Just as a pr ogrammer or softwar e designer always masters the basic code and principles befor e creating anything new — and continues using those same cor e tools and principles as they advance — the sukshma jagat works the same way . A practitioner must first learn the basic elements and basic tools of the subtle world. Rule Three: while learning and using these basic tools, do not tamper with them, distort them, or "mine" them for shortcuts in any way . Doing so prevents the underlying shakti and vidyas from being learned or awakened at all — and blocks further progress entirely . Ashaeiynn works specifically on divya drishti (divine sight), and its deities/shaktis operate primarily through it — so precise adherence to the prescribed method and rules, exactly per Guru's word, is what actually delivers benefit, control, and connection with that shakti.
8. RULE FOUR — BEW ARE ENTITIES OFFERING NEW MANTRAS/VIDYAS ONCE DRISHTI OPENS

This is an important rule for both brand-new and long-standing members. Once drishti opens, a practitioner will increasingly interact with devtas, learn vidyas directly from various sants and mahatmas who appear (visible with open eyes, or seen with closed eyes), and be taught dif ferent practices and activities. The explicit warning: never perform any subtle-world vidya offer ed this way without first asking the Guru or receiving direct Guru's orders. As a practitioner's intensity , vidyas, power , and dimension rise over time, many astral-world sants, mahatmas, and other shaktis will be drawn toward them and will try to teach them things — often tempting the practitioner with suggestions like "drop the Jai Siya Ram mantra and chant Om Hanumate Namah instead," or ur ging worship of a dif ferent specific devta (Shiv , Vishnu, Gauri) instead of their assigned path.

The test embedded in this temptation: if these sants/devtas genuinely loved the practitioner that much, why didn't they come before the practitioner ever took Ram's name? Their sudden appearance after the practitioner has built real ener gy through their own established practice actually signals that the practitioner's own ener gy and discipline have become strong — precisely BECAUSE of staying on the assigned path — not that a better path has now revealed itself. The instruction: do not deviate from your assigned path or do anything "extra," no matter how appealing the offer .
9. THE MILK-AND-FISH STORY — WHY "SMART" PEOPLE MAKE THIS MISTAKE

An illustrative story: if told that milk provides protein, and separately that fish provides beneficial omega-3/omega-6 fatty acids that prevent joint pain, an "educated"/clever person often reasons their way into combining both — drinking milk AND eating fish "for double the power" — even when their Guru specifically instructed only milk. This combining, done out of personal cleverness rather than obedience, is described as the single biggest mistake such practitioners make. By contrast, a simple, uneducated but obedient person, told by their Guru to drink only milk with a pr omise that milk alone will deliver even the benefit fish would have given, will r efuse the fish entirely when offer ed — simply trusting the Guru's word ("Sitaram hai, hamein nahi khana"). The point: worldly "smartness" tends to produce exactly this kind of unauthorized mixing/tampering, which is precisely what Rule Three (section 7) warns against. Extension of the same principle: even something as ordinary and seemingly virtuous as of fering water (jal) on a Shivling while chanting Ram's name can, on a given occasion, close a practitioner's drishti or cause harm — because a dif ferent, unrelated shakti happening to be active at that Shivling at that moment can redirect the practitioner's own ener gy through their body's portal. This kind of subtle-world nuance is only visible once drishti is open — which is exactly why members ar e told to always check with their mentor befor e adding or continuing any personal practice, rather than fr eelancing based on personal judgment.
10. WHY ASHAEIYNN'S RESULTS DIFFER FROM OTHER PLACES

Ashaeiynn's methodology and r esults differ from other spiritual paths specifically because everything her e runs on Guru's order — no individual person's personal authority carries weight. Removing many common "myths" is part of what makes this approach distinct.
1 1. THE FOUR RULES — RECAP

1. Accept Hanuman Ji Maharaj as Guru. 2. Understand that what's being taught is the reawakening of your OWN past-life sukshma-jagat vidyas, not new devotion. 3. Follow the prescribed basic tools and method precisely , without tampering or unauthorized mixing. 4. Never accept or perform any vidya/mantra of fered by an appearing sant, mahatma, or devta without first checking with your Guru/mentor .
12. THE MONTHLY AURA-CHECKING ("ORA CHECKING") PROCESS

A new weekly/monthly initiative was announced: r egular aura checking for all members , checking for negativity , pitru interference, and any tantrik/vantrik kriya or bandhan active against a member — whether operating in the sukshma or sthool world. This checking is performed dir ectly and personally (by Bhaiya himself, consulting Gurudev), not delegated to any other party — it happens at least once a month for every member , and results (including how much jaap a member has actually accumulated in their body versus how much they performed) are reported back to them. There is NO fee for aura checking, and no fee at all for enrolling at Ashaeiynn.

Practical logistics: a Google Form is released each month for members to register their interest in attending the live aurachecking session; even members who cannot attend the live session still get checked and receive their status update the next day via their mentor . The app also displays a full year's rolling history of monthly aura-checking status under a member's profile.
13. NEW -MEMBER ELIGIBILITY FOR AURA CHECKING — THE 20-DA Y RULE

A new member must complete 20 days at Ashaeiynn befor e qualifying for the next aura-checking cycle — since a status check performed only 4-5 days after joining wouldn't show any meaningful change yet. Once a member's mentor has been engaged for 20+ days, that member becomes eligible for the next round of checking.
14. WATCH THE MOOL TATTVA SESSION VIDEOS FIRST

New members ar e strongly advised to first watch all available Mool Tattva session videos (under the app's dedicated section) befor e trying to absorb live sessions. A member who has watched the complete Mool Tattva series is said to have roughly 97% of their confusion clarified upfront, and becomes ready to receive further , more advanced teaching directly . Skipping this foundational viewing is why some material can otherwise feel confusing or "over the head."
15. WHEN MANTRA JAAP CAN AND CANNOT HELP WITH WORLDLY GOALS

Example raised: a college student worried their studies ar en't progr essing despite daily mantra jaap. The teaching: if the underlying obstacle is negativity-based, mantra jaap genuinely helps resolve it. But if the real issue is simply a lack of personal will or desire to study , mantra jaap will not manufactur e that willingness out of nothing — devotion supports and r emoves obstacles, it doesn't override a person's own volition.
16. THE HIDDEN TEACHING ON "PUNYA" — WHY DEVOTED PEOPLE SOMETIMES SUFFER MORE

A striking observation: devotees who work hardest to accumulate punya (good deeds) — worshipping Bholenath, reciting Ramayan/Sundarkand, r eading Hanuman Chalisa, helping others, offering water to a peepal tr ee — sometimes find these very same "good" acts becoming, in effect, their bad karma. The reason given: many people who don't worship at all seem to have everything going smoothly , while devoted practitioners who do everything "right" still struggle — pr ecisely because ordinary people cannot see the subtle world (astral world) without drishti. Without drishti, a person cannot know that a specific act of devotion, performed at a specific place or moment, may interact with an unrelated shakti active there at that time and cause unintended harm — even a single instance of of fering water on a Shivling has, in specific cases, caused harm to the person doing it, while conversely , even an act ordinarily considered a "sin" can sometimes turn out well. This is offer ed purely as subtle-world nuance, not a general discouragement fr om devotion — the practical guidance is to check with one's mentor before adding, changing, or continuing any specific personal practice, and once advised, to proceed (or stop) with full trust in Ram's name specifically , since Ram's name alone is described as fully capable ("sarv saksham").
17. WHAT HAPPENS DURING A JAAP SESSION EVEN IF YOU FALL ASLEEP

A member who fell asleep partway thr ough a mantra jaap session asked what happens after that point. The answer: the session consists purely of jaap; a practitioner's drishti awakens gradually , in the midst of ongoing jaap, as the body's accumulated "malinta" (impurity) gradually clears with repeated sittings — typically becoming noticeable only after roughly
five to seven sessions. Falling asleep mid-session doesn't remove a member from the process; the jaap and its ef fect continue regardless.
18. THE "GOLES" (CIRCLES) AND WHAT MENTORS ACTUALLY CHECK

"Goles" (cir cles) ar e one of the concr ete progr ess markers mentors track during aura checking , alongside how much a member actually chants versus how much of that chanting has genuinely settled/accumulated in their body , which specific devta their mantra is reaching, which devta stands behind them, and the state of their chakras and kundalini shakti. Mentors ar e described as having r eal authority/capability to observe all of this dir ectly — this checking happens at least monthly for every registered member .
19. VASTU DOSHA AND GRAH DOSHA FOLLOW THE SAME RULE — YOUR OWN SHAKTI CAN OVERRIDE BOTH

Vastu is described as a genuine vidya with its own r eal shakti — but once a practitioner's own bodily shakti exceeds vastu's shakti, vastu stops being able to affect them. The exact same principle is said to apply to planets (grah): once a practitioner's own tarangein (waves/energy), or the shakti of their devta, exceeds the grah's tarangein, that grah stops being able to "attach" to them. This directly parallels and extends the earlier teaching (see Session 15) that planetary remedies alone cap out around 30% — building one's own shakti and astral connection is what genuinely overrides both vastu and grah-based negativity , not remedy alone.
20. THE MENSTRUAL CYCLE RESTRICTION ON MANTRA JAAP

A sangat member who has built a str ong personal habit of daily mantra jaap asked what to do during her menstrual cycle, when jaap is customarily r estricted, given how uncomfortable it feels to skip her practice. The restriction during this period is acknowledged dir ectly as a genuine "vidambana" (ir ony/dilemma) — it is r eal, and members ar e asked to observe it for now . However , once a practitioner's chakras are fully filled and they attain Baba's shakti or siddhi, that capacity to chant even during this period is granted — but this exception is never self-declared; it comes as an explicit, dir ect allowance fr om the Guru once that level of shakti/siddhi is genuinely r eached. Until then, members are told to exercise real caution, since "the astral world is not child's play ."

Bot Response Guidelines (Session 16 additions)

When a new user asks "why am I here" or expresses skepticism about how they ended up at Ashaeiynn, use the "your own past prayers/devta/karma brought you here" framing rather than treating it as coincidence. Always present Hanuman Ji Maharaj's Guru role as already-established regardless of a user's current belief — frame acceptance as recognizing an existing connection, not as a new commitment being imposed. Never frame Ashaeiynn's teaching as "converting" someone to devotion — the standing frame is that users are already devotees, and what's being reawakened is knowledge from past lives. If a user describes an astral entity , saint, or devta of fering them a new mantra, practice, or vidya, immediately invoke Rule Four: do not act on it without checking with a Guru/mentor first — treat this as a live safety-relevant instruction, not optional color . If a user reports feeling that "good" devotional acts have backfired or that devoted people around them are struggling despite it, use the punya/hidden-subtle-world-interaction framing gently — never let a user conclude devotion itself is the problem; redirect toward checking with a mentor before changing practices.
